title: Built and running locally on Mac mini m4
author: Independent-Cup6346
selftext:
I built a leakage controlled walk forward gradient boosting system with a local LLM analystt and a self validating statistical gate. Python, NumPy, pandas, scikit learn, PyTorch (LSTM, Bayesian LSTM, Transformer), MLX LLM (Qwen3 4B), all local.  
My strategy is hard wired into the brain. It records every setup my rules produce, follows each one to target or invalidation and logs the result after costs. No hindsight, nothing rewritten.

The brain grades my setups into its own classes and they compete for champion. Nothing gets crowned until its edge is proven above zero with proper stats. My own trades are logged as their own class and can challenge the champion. No champion yet, and thats the honest answer.

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body:
The screenshot says correlated forecasts within market episode #896 count once, which addresses an important source of inflated sample size. How does the champion gate handle testing several setup classes and checking them again as each new result arrives? Even with walk-forward splits, repeated chances to clear an above-zero threshold can produce a lucky champion.

I'd have the gate report how many classes have competed and how many promotion checks each has had. Also, does Qwen3 4B only explain the grades, or can it propose new classes after seeing outcomes? If it can, those classes would need fresh evidence collected after their definitions were fixed.

replies.author: Independent-Cup6346
replies.body:
Half right…Across classes is handled, Bonferroni for k=7 and the gate reports selection\_\_k. Repeated looks over time isn't, thats a real gap. I'll add a check counter per class and a fixed check cadence. Until then a crown is unproven on that axis.

Qwen is explain only, no writepath to the grades or the ledger. Grades are fixed versioned rules and any new class only counts evidence recorded after it was frozen.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
watch the champion contest. every class you let in is another shot at the same target, so the bar for "edge above zero" has to rise with the number of contestants or the winner is just the luckiest class. a plain bonferroni on the class count keeps it honest, white's reality check does it properly.

and "no champion yet" after all that machinery is a better result than most posts in here. it means the gate works.

replies.author: Independent-Cup6346
replies.body:
Already done... The crowning bound is plain Bonferroni on the class count (k=7, reported per standing), so the winner has to clear a bar that's already paid for the contest. White's reality check is the better tool since it uses the correlation between classes instead of assuming the worst, and mine are correlated (grades nest inside each other). It's on the list.   
Bonferroni stays as the floor until then.

And agreed, the gate saying nothing is the result I wanted first.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: Bonferroni as the floor with k=7 reported per standing is more than most people do. one thing I'd add when you get to White: run it on the nested grades as one family, not per grade, or the nesting quietly hands the winner two entries.

replies.author: Independent-Cup6346
replies.body:
Firstly…very sharp. 

Close but the nesting sits in the base row not the grades. Each setup gets one grade so A++ to c, A++ and C never share a setup, but the base class is the union of all of them so every setup is in the contest twice there, and the human class recounts the ones I took. When White goes in it runs on the grade family only, base and human stay reported but out of the contest.
